editorial.headline: A Mobile Drinks Trade That Is Open Nationally but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This prepared-drink activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s registration structure prevents a PT PMA from registering it today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 56306 concerns a particular kind of beverage service: drinks are made before sale, served ready to drink, and ordinarily sold while the provider moves from place to place. The scope explicitly captures mobile sellers of ice doger, ice cincau and jamu. That combination is important: preparation and immediate service belong to the activity, alongside mobility. It is defined both by the beverage’s ready-to-drink condition and by the absence of a fixed selling place.

The scale setting is equally specific. The record opens the activity to Mikro and Kecil businesses. That makes the scale classification more than an administrative footnote: it is the frame through which this mobile prepared-drink activity is made available for registration. Founders should read scope and scale together: what is being offered is an on-the-move service for drinks made for consumption, and its stated registration scales are Mikro and Kecil. The stated scales define the registration boundary as given; neither the ready-to-drink nature of the product nor the mobile method of sale removes it.

At the national level, the position is clear. PMA status is TERBUKA and the permitted foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, so the national listing allows full foreign ownership. For someone assessing investment nationally, the point is unambiguous: foreign participation is not merely permitted in part; the stated ceiling reaches the whole capital position. It is a national statement, however—not a promise that every provincial registration path remains available.

Bali changes the conclusion decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today through a PT PMA. The Bali record marks it Closed to PMA (no Besar scale) because OSS has no Usaha Besar scale row: the activity is reserved for UMKM, while a PT PMA is Usaha Besar by law. The record also identifies a permanent, island-wide provincial PMA block for low and medium-low risk KBLI. This is a structural restriction, not an editorial caveat: it determines whether an applicant can use the PT PMA form at all. Whether the national listing is fully open is therefore not the practical answer on the island; the local registration structure blocks the PT PMA route outright.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open at 100% foreign ownership does not make the PT PMA registration route available in Bali.
